continuity: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar, original 1985 Commodore 64 manual witness
work_or_witness: Origin Systems, The History of Britannia
description: The sovereign who unites the mainland and nearby islands under Britannia, rules its major continent, and declares the Quest of the Avatar in search of a person who can exemplify a new standard for the nation.

roles_and_vocations.note: The manual says Lord British united the mainland/islands under one rule and rules Britannia; EA calls him the Quest's proclaimer.

affiliations.note: Named realm of Lord British's rule; retained as a place/affiliation term, never an endpoint.
Lord British describes the Quest in the manual's afterword.

cosmologies_and_realms.note: The manual identifies Lord British as its ruler and situates his castle on its central continent.

metaphysical_laws_and_rituals.note: The manual says earlier seekers achieved enlightenment in one or more Virtues and describes the Quest's target state; no personal Avatar status is assigned to Lord British.

canon_status: Named individual directly profiled in the original Origin 1985 manual and corroborated by EA's official product premise.

citations.locator: The History of Britannia, pp. 3–4 and 36–37
supports: Lord British's unification/rule of Britannia and first-person Quest of the Avatar statement
Lord British's proclamation of the Quest and spiritual-example purpose

comparison_cautions: This is Lord British as presented in the scoped Ultima IV manual, not a claim about all series appearances, creator persona, historical reconstructions, or later retcons.
His in-world account and aspirational Quest language are not treated as exhaustive political history or proof of each seeker's outcome.
